title: Axiomatic PausePoint Controller for Deterministic Rollback and Replay
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We continue to see classes of partial-canary exposures where user sessions observe mixed model states after an interrupted rollout or an incident-driven rollback. This PR introduces an axiomatic PausePoint concept and a PausePoint Controller that provides deterministic, replayable checkpoints for staged rollouts so that rollbacks and replays restore session-consistent behavior across cohorts.

What this PR does (single-line description): Adds a controller + runtime hook that captures compact traffic snapshots (PausePoints), exposes an API to advance/hold rollouts at named pausepoints, and enables deterministic replay/rollback with provenance metadata and automated safety gates.

Highlights: - PausePoint primitives: named checkpoints that record cohort boundaries, KV cache cursors, and deterministic nonce info so replay yields the same routing and KV state for affected sessions. - Controller: declarative PausePoint resources (CRD-style in Redwood control plane) with accept/hold/rewind actions, integrated with existing rollout schedules and canary policies. - Replay/rollback API: atomic rewind operation replays traffic for the snapshotted window (optionally sampled) to validate behavior before committing a rollback, with idempotency guarantees and bounded reordering. - Telemetry & gates: snapshot-scoped metrics emitted to the Console, automatic evaluation against configured SLO gates, and optional human latch for high-risk rollbacks. - Backwards compatibility: runtime falls back to existing shadow/canary logic when PausePoint metadata is missing.

Design notes: - PausePoints are intentionally compact (checksum + lightweight cursor + cohort signature) to avoid large storage overhead and to support cross-region replication. - Replays are performed using a determinism-first scheduler: same request ordering for replayed subset, deterministic pseudorandom seeds for model-side sampling tokens, and replay isolation (no external side-effects are committed unless the rollback is approved). - Safety-first: Rewinds always run in a sandboxed verification lane and produce a diff report; automated rollback only triggers when metric gates cross configured thresholds or with manual approval.

Migration & rollout plan: - Control plane stores PausePoint metadata in the rollout database (no schema migration for model manifests). - Gradual rollout: operator flag to enable PausePoint behaviour per cluster; default disabled for 2 weeks while we gather real traffic snapshots in Canary mode. - Known limitations: currently does not capture external downstream side-effects (webhooks, DB writes) — those require application-level compensating logic.

Why now: several recent incidents where partial canary promotion caused user-visible inconsistency motivated an explicit, auditable checkpoint primitive so operators can deterministically roll back and validate replays without relying on ad-hoc logs or full traffic recapture.

Related work: complements the existing staged-rollout and shadow frameworks (see ENG-4982, pr-71234 and pr-96342 for prior canary safety work).

merge_commit_message: Axiomatic PausePoint Controller: add controller, runtime hook, console report; enables deterministic snapshot+replay for rollouts. Closes ENG-4982.
release_notes: Introduces PausePoints: a lightweight checkpoint primitive for deterministic rollback and replay. Operators can create named pausepoints to capture cohort-consistent snapshots and perform sandboxed replays to validate rollbacks before committing. Opt-in via operator flag; consult docs/ops/pausepoints.md for migration steps and limitations.
